title: Runway Priming & Bento Mix: micro-run log
content:
Context:
Quick personal log experimenting with a lightweight "runway priming" pattern intended to reduce cold-path p95/p99 during short windows of high QPS (~30s to 3m). The idea: inject a small, targeted sequence of warmup calls (short prefills + control requests) ahead of an expected surge to bring the model/kv cache/GPU into the steady-state fast-path with minimal cost.

Why "Bento mix"?
I used the term to describe a compact, repeatable mixture of request shapes (tiny, medium, long) that matches our real client fingerprint in a single payload set. Bento = mix of flavors so we don't overfit warmup to a single token length.

Hypotheses:
- A 6-request runway priming (2 tiny, 3 medium, 1 long) within 10s prior to surge reduces p99 by 25-40% compared to no priming for 60s surges.
- KV prefix hits correlate strongly with p95 improvements; small synthetic prefills that align prefix tokens with expected user starts are most valuable.
- Aggressive batch_timeout reductions during the runway window may hurt throughput but reduce tail latency; tradeoff worth it for short windows.

Experiment setup (single-node emulation):
- Model: open-llama-13b-ggml-qat (quantized variant we use in the lab).
- Hardware: single A10G-equivalent node emulated with our microclient harness.
- Arrival: sawtooth ramp 0 -> 120 qps over 10s, hold 60s, decay 10s. Also tested Poisson jitter overlay (sigma=0.12).
- Request mix (Bento): tiny=32 tokens, medium=128 tokens, long=512 tokens, 60% tiny+medium, 40% long (sampled).
- Configs tested: baseline (no priming), runway-priming (6 calls, 10s before), priming+batch_timeout=5ms, priming+kv-prefix-prefill (prefill with first 16 tokens).
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_hit_rate, GPU util, tokens/sec, observed batching size distribution, tail-sample traces.

Raw observations:
- Baseline p99 at peak: ~1.48s. p95 ~0.62s. p50 ~0.09s.
- Runway priming alone: p99 dropped to ~0.94s (-36%), p95 ~0.45s (-27%), p50 unchanged. KV hit-rate increased from 11% -> 38% during the first 25s of surge window.
- Priming + batch_timeout=5ms: p99 ~0.78s (-47% baseline), but tokens/sec dropped ~8% (some throughput loss due to smaller batch coalescing).
- Priming + kv-prefix-prefill: p99 ~0.72s, kv_hit_rate ~52% at start of surge, best tail improvement but highest extra cost in token-priming (~0.6 additional token-cost per real request amortized).
- Poisson jitter test: runway priming is robust to +/- 0.2*mean jitter; beyond that benefit decays unless priming window moved closer to surge.

Tracing note (stripes in traces):
- When priming preceded surge by >20s benefits drop off quickly. Fine-grained timing matters — the "golden window" is ~3-12s before ramp.
- Long requests sometimes unblock batches and create temporary KV eviction pressure; prefer prefilling short tokens first, then medium, then long.

Quick cost/benefit (back-of-envelope):
- Extra token-cost from 6-call priming: ~30 tokens average = tiny relative to cost of p99 tail (customer impact).
- Throughput loss from reduced batch coalescing (in batch_timeout variant) is measurable but acceptable for short windows and high-tail-sensitivity customers.

Recommendations / next steps:
1) Add a configurable "runway_priming_profile" in the runtime with parameters: priming_sequence (list of sizes), lead_time_s, batch_mode (allow-slower-coalesce true/false), prefix_prefill boolean.
2) Build an automated scheduler in Console to trigger a runway profile for predictable events (cron-like) and an API to trigger on demand (webhook from app).
3) Run fleet-scale multitenant experiments to confirm no cross-tenant eviction side-effects. Need to capture eviction rates and cold-path re-enqueue counts.
4) For now, enable priming+kv-prefix for enterprise customers with tail-SLOs; expose expected cost delta in the Console.

Open questions / To investigate:
- How does runway priming interact with model-variant switching (e.g., warm to quantized variant fallback)?
- Does token compression / merging at ingress reduce priming efficacy?
- Can we synthesize a micro-priming signal with zero extra token-cost using ephemeral internal cache markers?

Notes to self: replicate with Dedicated pool (multi-GPU) and with private deployment networking; record GPU slice wake latency as an additional metric. Also try a shorter 3-call micro-runway for sub-30s surges.

Scratch checklist (for follow-on run):
- [ ] implement harness change to emit per-request prefix tokens to KV monitor
- [ ] add automated timing sweep to find golden window for varying surge durations
- [ ] instrument eviction counters into telemetry dashboard
- [ ] draft small Confluence explainer with gifs and timing diagrams

End of log.
summary: Personal experiment notes exploring a small "runway priming" warmup sequence (Bento request mix) to reduce p99 during short surges. Observed p99 reductions up to ~50% with a small token cost and modest throughput tradeoffs; next steps include fleet testing and Console integration.
